import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# 1. Load and filter datasets for task_id == 103, drop missing values
df_pos = pd.read_parquet('train.parquet')
df_pos = df_pos[df_pos['task_id'] == 103][['QED_delta', 'MW_delta', 'action_type']].dropna()

df_neg = pd.read_parquet('train_neg.parquet')
df_neg = df_neg[df_neg['task_id'] == 103][['QED_delta', 'MW_delta', 'action_type']].dropna()

# Label success
df_pos['success'] = 1
df_neg['success'] = 0
# Combine
df = pd.concat([df_pos, df_neg], ignore_index=True)

# 2. Compute ratio = |QED_delta| / |MW_delta|, exclude zero MW_delta
epsilon = 1e-6
df = df[df['MW_delta'].abs() > epsilon].copy()
df['ratio'] = df['QED_delta'].abs() / df['MW_delta'].abs()

# 3. Summary statistics by success group
group_stats = df.groupby('success')['ratio'].agg(count='count', mean='mean', std='std')
print("Summary of |QED_delta|/|MW_delta| by success group:")
print(group_stats, "\n")

# 4. Welch two-sample t-test
ratio_succ = df.loc[df['success'] == 1, 'ratio']
ratio_fail = df.loc[df['success'] == 0, 'ratio']
t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(ratio_succ, ratio_fail, equal_var=False)
print(f"Welch t-test: t = {t_stat:.4f}, p = {p_val:.4e}\n")

# 5. OLS regression: ratio ~ success + C(action_type)
model = smf.ols('ratio ~ success + C(action_type)', data=df).fit()
coef = model.params['success']
se = model.bse['success']
pv = model.pvalues['success']
ci_lower, ci_upper = model.conf_int().loc['success']
print("Regression result for 'success' effect on ratio:")
print(f"coef = {coef:.4f}, SE = {se:.4f}, p = {pv:.4e}")
print(f"95% CI = [{ci_lower:.4f}, {ci_upper:.4f}]\n")

# 6. Plot distributions
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
sns.violinplot(x='success', y='ratio', data=df, palette='Set2')
plt.xticks([0,1], ['Failure', 'Success'])
plt.ylabel('|QED_delta| / |MW_delta|')
plt.title('Normalized effect size by success status')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

- OLS regression (ratio ~ success + action_type): success coef = 0.0322 (SE=0.0036), p = 2.72×10⁻¹⁹, 95% CI [0.0252, 0.0393]
- Violin plot shows failures clustered near zero and successes with a broader, higher distribution.

Conclusion: The experiment was implemented as planned and shows that successful edits in the drug-likeness task have a significantly higher normalized effect size than failures.","success":true}
